your_book:
Wednesday's session left Jaleel's $23,970 book essentially treading water at the portfolio level — unrealized gains sit at $1,094 (+4.78%) — but the day had sharp cross-currents underneath. NVDA was the standout winner, surging +3.43% to $1,430, while Danaher added +2.51% to $1,398; both provided meaningful lift. On the other side, UBER cratered -5.29% to $1,091 — the single worst day move in the book — with no company-specific catalyst visible in the data, suggesting macro or sector-rotation pressure. BSX dropped another -2.75% to $1,193, ZTS fell -2.17% to $2,455, and GILD shed -2.58%, compounding an already uncomfortable picture in the healthcare sleeve.

The drift problem is concentrated and worth naming plainly. RKLB remains the largest single position at 15.6% of the book ($3,741) yet carries an AVOID verdict and a -4.5% open loss — price and thesis are fully disconnected. UBER is rated STRONG BUY with a QARP of 77.6 but sits at a -4.8% loss and just took a -5.29% session hit. BSX and ZTS are both STRONG BUY-rated names sitting in the red on cost basis while their underlying risk flags (BSX guidance slashed, ZTS session weakness) deserve scrutiny. SPGI is down -4.9% from cost on a BUY verdict — another wedge to monitor.

Software held up relatively well: ADBE added +0.71%, SAP +0.94%, and NOW slipped only -0.78% despite the rotation narrative benefiting the group broadly. The Microsoft earnings event after the close could move NOW and ADBE on Thursday. The NVDA headline mentioning Michael Burry's 'ghost town' framing is noise for now but worth tracking given the export-control risk flag already on file. Next hard date to watch: NVDA reports August 26.

attention.headline: Largest position carries AVOID verdict and open loss
attention.note: At 15.6% of the book ($3,741) with a -4.5% loss and an AVOID rating, RKLB is the clearest position-sizing contradiction in the portfolio — a capital-preservation mandate is hard to square with this much concentration in a name the model explicitly flags to avoid.

attention.headline: -5.29% session drop on no visible company catalyst
attention.note: A STRONG BUY-rated name with QARP 77.6 just had its worst session in the book with no earnings or news trigger provided — the gap between the conviction rating and the price action is widening and warrants watching for a confirming reason.

attention.headline: STRONG BUY but guidance was slashed and stock fell -2.75% today
attention.note: BSX's FY26 growth was cut from 10.5% to 7–8.5% with management guiding flat through Q3; today's -2.75% session move on top of a -0.3% open loss means the risk flag is actively translating into price pressure, not just sitting on paper.

attention.headline: Biggest dollar loser on the day at -2.17% with no flag resolution
attention.note: ZTS is the second-largest position at $2,455, rated STRONG BUY with a high QARP of 84.6, yet sits at a -5.5% loss on cost and shed the most dollar value in the book today — the conviction is high but the price continues to move the wrong direction without a clear catalyst in the data.
